learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to predict and analyze the flight dynamic behavior of a fixed-wing aircraft based on geometric properties and to independently derive and interpret the relevant equations.
Students can name the safety requirements of a passenger aircraft and independently derive the safety budgets of individual aircraft systems.
Students are able to predict the failure probability of a system, as well as an aircraft crash or maintenance incident, based on the system's architecture.
Students are able to optimize the safety level of an aircraft system through technical measures.

syllabus_topics: Safety and real-time requirements for avionics systems
Basic structure and functional principles of avionics systems
Mathematical models for calculating the failure probability of individual aircraft systems
Analysis methods for evaluating the effects of failure on the aircraft
Protective measures for such systems in relation to environmental effects and random errors
Coordinate and reference systems of an aircraft

assessment_methods.method: Exam (written or oral) or presentation for MECB611C
Exam (written or oral) or presentation for MECB612C

assessment_rules: The examination performance is taken in two individual examinations. The weighting is equal for both events according to CP. The module grade MECB610C results from the grades of MECB611C and MECB612C with equal weighting. For MECB611C, a graded written exam (60 min) or graded oral exam (20 min) or graded presentation (20 min) is required. For MECB612C, a graded written exam (60 min) or graded oral exam (20 min) or graded presentation (20 min) is required.
bibliography: Stephen Corda; Introduction to Aerospace Engineering
